title: Quarterly Roadmap: Private Instances Sprint Catalog, OKR Traceability & Failure Mode Budget
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Objective: Create a concise, executable quarterly roadmap artifact for Private/VPC/On‑Prem capabilities that maps sprints to OKRs, specifies rollout gates, and allocates a Failure Mode Budget (FMB) for enterprise customers. This ticket produces a sprint catalog (4 sprints) with measurable acceptance criteria, cross‑functional owners, and escalation runbooks.

Context: Multiple Q1 signals suggest enterprise customers are onboarding into Private deployments faster than forecast. We need a lightweight but operational roadmap to: (1) prioritize compatibility and stability work, (2) preserve SLAs during model/runtime upgrades, and (3) provide customers clear expectations for upgrade windows and risk tolerance. The FMB concept defines how many degraded requests/incidents we accept across the quarter before delaying noncritical feature rollouts.

What this artifact contains: sprint-by-sprint catalog mapping to OKRs, success metrics, owner for each backlog slice, explicit rollout gate conditions, automated rollback thresholds, and a minimal oncall/escalation playbook. Includes links to runbooks, compliance checklist, and an executive summary for GTM.

Primary trade-offs considered: prioritizing stability fixes vs. new feature delivery; trade budget across Dedicated vs. Private lanes; conservative FMB reduces release velocity but lowers customer SLA risk.

Deliverables: single JSON roadmap artifact suitable for consumption by console release manager and engineering leads, a one-page executive summary for Sales/CS, and a list of gated tickets for enforcement in CI.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Sprint catalog lists 4 sprints with objective, top-3 backlog items, owners, and estimates
A2: Each sprint maps to at least one OKR key result and a measurable metric (uptime, p95 latency, upgrade success rate)
A3: Failure Mode Budget defined numerically with enforcement rules and automated alerts wired to SRE oncall
A4: Rollout gates codified (canary cohorts, fallback model variant, rollback triggers) and documented in runbook link
A5: Stakeholder signoff (Product, Eng, Security, Solutions) captured in comments and executive summary delivered
